title: Blest Who with Generous Pity Glows
description: Blest Who with Generous Pity Glows in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 780 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Blessedness of considering the Poor. Ps. 41:1-3”, where the book credits them to Pratt's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest who with gen-erous pi-ty glows, Who learns to feel an-oth-er's woes; Bows to the poor man's wants his ear, And wipes the help-less or-phan's tear! In ev-ery want, in ev-ery woe, Him-self thy pi-ty, Lord, shall know.

lines: Blest who with generous pity glows,
Who learns to feel another's woes;
Bows to the poor man's wants his ear,
And wipes the helpless orphan's tear!
In every want, in every woe,
Himself thy pity, Lord, shall know.
Thy love his life shall guard, thy hand
Give to his lot the chosen land;
Nor leave him, in the troubled day,
In sickness thou shall raise his head,
And make with tenderest care his bed.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
